sentences.text: This Petition has been filed to dispense with the production of the certified copy of the order dated 29.07.2025 passed in Crl.M.P.No.6933 of 2025 in S.C.No.320 of 2022 on the file of the learned Sessions Judge, Mahila Court, Allikulam.
The aforesaid order in Crl.MP.No.6933 of 2025 dated 29.07.2025 has been passed thereby dismissing the petition filed for seeking to to recall some of the prosecution side witnesses 2.

The petitioner is the accused facing charges for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 509,
376, 511 and 506(ii) of IPC r/w Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act.

entities.text: Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is alleged in the complaint that the petitioner and the victim participated in a Junior Judo Championship competition held in Namakkal and after participating in the competition, while they were returning to Erode Railway Station by car, the accused committed sexual assault on the victim.
Hence, the aforementioned complaint was registered in Crime No.5 of 2021 against the petitioner for the offences stated supra.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Advocate(crl.side)
appearing for the first respondent and perused, all the materials available on record.
4.
It is seen that the prosecution examined their witnesses and when the matter was posted for judgment, the petitioner filed the above referred petition to recall some of the prosecution witnesses.

It is noted that the petitioner https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
08/08/2025 05:43:12 pm ) already filed a petition in Crl.MP.No.2458 of 2025 to recall the prosecution witnesses.
However, the same was dismissed on 24.03.2025.
Subsequently, the petitioner has filed a criminal original petition in Crl.O.P.No.16762 of 2025 before this Court, which is now pending.
It is seen that the petitioner is regularly taking adjournment and also filing memo to drag the proceedings.
Now, the petitioner has once again filed the recall petition for the very same prayer, which is nothing but clear abuse of process of Court of law and dragging the proceedings.

5. In view of the above discussion, this Court is not inclined to dispense with the production of the certified copy of the order dated 29.07.2025 passed in Crl.M.P.No.6933 of 2025 in S.C.No.320 of 2022 on the file of the learned Sessions Judge, Mahila Court, Allikulam.
Accordingly, this Criminal Miscellaneous Petition is dismissed.
Consequently, the connected Criminal Revision Case is rejected at the SR stage itself.
